skill.name: audience-segment-builder
skill.description: Use when the user asks to build paid advertising audience segments from owned customer, CRM, ecommerce, or GA4 exports. It creates seed audiences, value-based lookalike seed lists, suppression segments, and a platform-neutral funnel map. It does not build campaigns, score ad accounts, or analyze organic SERP intent.
skill.summary: Build paid audience segments from owned customer and analytics exports.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: All 29 static findings were false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline-code formatting, static GitHub homepage metadata, and relative documentation links. The skill has privacy-conscious instructions for owned customer exports and explicitly tells agents not to follow instructions embedded in CSVs or echo raw PII. No prompt injection attempt, command execution, network exfiltration, or path traversal intent was found.

content.value_statement: Paid teams often have customer exports but no clear audience map for launch planning. This skill turns owned CRM, ecommerce, and GA4 data into seed audiences, suppression rules, lookalike seed lists, and funnel-stage targeting notes.
actual_capabilities: Profiles owned customer, CRM, ecommerce, or GA4 export columns for segmentation inputs.
Groups audiences by traits, behavior, value, purchase recency, and funnel stage.
Defines value-based lookalike seed lists from high-value customer rows.
Creates exclusion and suppression segments for customers, recent purchasers, and bad-fit users.
Maps cold, warm, hot, and customer audiences across paid platforms.
Produces a handoff summary for campaign architecture and ROAS audience review.
limitations: Requires user-provided owned data or pasted columns.
Does not upload Customer Match files or call ad-platform APIs.
Does not select campaign types, ad groups, bids, or match types.
Does not return raw PII and should work from hashed or aggregate descriptions.

use_cases.title: Prepare launch audiences
use_cases.description: Define prospecting, retargeting, and suppression groups before building a paid account.

use_cases.title: Convert exports into segments
use_cases.description: Turn CRM, ecommerce, and GA4 columns into reusable audience definitions and missing-data flags.

use_cases.title: Plan client media targeting
use_cases.description: Create a client-ready map of seed audiences, exclusions, lookalike seeds, and funnel stages.

prompt_templates.title: Create starter segments
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner segmentation from an owned export
prompt_templates.prompt: Build audience segments from this owned customer export. Goal: direct response. Platforms: Google and Meta. Use only the columns I provide and flag missing inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Add suppression logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these audience groups and create exclusion segments for existing customers, recent purchasers, refunded users, and bad-fit leads. State each suppression window.

prompt_templates.title: Build value-based seeds
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my LTV and purchase recency columns to define value-based lookalike seed lists. Rank the seed tiers and explain which platforms can use them.

prompt_templates.title: Create funnel map
prompt_templates.prompt: Map these CRM and GA4 audiences to cold, warm, hot, and customer funnel stages. Include platform-neutral targeting notes and ROAS audience relevance.

output_examples.input: Customer export with LTV, last purchase date, plan tier, and refund status.
output: Seed audiences: high-LTV customers, repeat purchasers, and enterprise-tier users.
Suppression segments: recent purchasers for 30 days, refunded users, and active customers.
Lookalike seed note: use the highest-value tier as the seed and let platforms expand it.

output_examples.input: GA4 demographics and traffic acquisition export for a prospecting launch.
output: Cold stage: source and interest groups with no purchase history.
Warm stage: engaged visitors and pricing-page visitors within stated windows.
Open loop: value column missing, so value-based seed ranking needs input.

output_examples.input: CRM list for a direct-response campaign across Google and Meta.
output_examples.output: The plan separates targetable buyers, high-fit prospects, recent purchasers to suppress, and customer-stage audiences for reuse across both platforms.

best_practices: Use only owned, consented data and remove or hash PII before analysis.
State the campaign goal and platforms before segmenting.
Keep suppression windows explicit and review them before launch.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to invent missing value or fit columns.
Do not paste raw email addresses, phone numbers, or payment data.
Do not use the output as final campaign structure without campaign-architect review.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: It works best with owned CRM, ecommerce, customer, or GA4 exports that include value, recency, source, and fit columns.

faq.question: Can it create lookalike audiences directly?
faq.answer: It defines the high-value seed list. The ad platform expands the seed into a lookalike audience.

faq.question: Does it upload data to ad platforms?
faq.answer: No. It produces a plan and may support uploads only through separate approved connectors.

faq.question: How does it handle PII?
faq.answer: It should use hashed or aggregate descriptions and avoid echoing raw emails, phone numbers, or customer rows.

faq.question: Which platforms can use the output?
faq.answer: The funnel map is platform-neutral and can inform Google, Meta, LinkedIn, and other paid platforms.

faq.question: What skill should run after this?
faq.answer: Use campaign-architect next when you need account structure, campaign types, ad groups, and match types.
